pathway.title: VSE CORP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. VSE has levered up through an equity-heavy acquisition, and its leverage path is mostly a matter of earnings timing. Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA against 1.24x at December 2025 [CP-1 leverage chart; S7 page:7], because the trailing earnings include only five months of the acquired business while all of its debt is on the balance sheet. Management's full-year 2026 guidance of revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.9% to 19.1% [S7 page:3] implies full-year Adjusted EBITDA of about USD 347 million to USD 354 million (calculated below), which would put net debt at about 2.6x on a flat net debt. This is a mechanical, not a proven, deleveraging, and it relies on guidance that the filings do not yet evidence (Analyst Interpretation on a Management Language basis). The credit implication is that leverage tolerance is acceptable if the guided run-rate is delivered and thin if the acquired earnings disappoint.

2. VSE's liquidity and maturity profile make near-term default or refinancing risk low. Cash of USD 65.8 million and unused revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million total USD 545.0 million against USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months, and annual scheduled principal is no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031, with the balance of the term loan due from 2032, mostly at its 2033 maturity [CP-1 maturity wall; S4 page:19]. The risk mechanic that remains is acquisition spending: the revolver helps fund bolt-on deals (Atech, acquired on 2026-08-31, was funded with cash and revolver borrowings, and USD 20.0 million was drawn at 2026-09-30 [S4 page:9 and page:17]) so liquidity can fall if acquisitions continue before free cash flow turns up.

3. Cash conversion is the weak spot. Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months and free cash flow negative USD 3.4 million, after a USD 148.4 million inventory build [CP-1; S4 page:6], while Q3 2026 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million. Growth programs, including the new OEM auxiliary power unit program the Company names [S4 page:33], absorb inventory ahead of revenue. The credit implication is that debt reduction comes from year-end working capital release and earnings, not from structural cash generation shown so far; the write-down of slow-moving inventories was a critical audit matter in FY2025 [S1 page:40].

4. VSE's cost of debt is floating and only partly hedged. Secured floating debt is USD 917.75 million with USD 250.0 million of swaps, leaving about USD 667.8 million exposed; each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest, about 2.2% of trailing adjusted EBITDA (calculated below). Trailing adjusted EBITDA covers contractual annual interest of USD 57.7 million 5.20x. Cash interest cover cannot be shown for 2026 because cash interest is not reported (FY2025 was 6.81x) [CP-1].

5. The business risks are concentration and dependence on OEMs. One affiliated customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and its post-acquisition share is not disclosed [CP-1A; S1 page:11]; repair, now 58.8% of Q3 2026 revenue, depends on OEM approvals and licenses such as the Pratt & Whitney PT6 fuel pump license [CP-1A; S4 page:14]. The mechanism is that the loss of the group or an approval removes high-margin work while inventory and capacity remain. The implication is that earnings quality is exposed to two single points of failure whose terms are not in the pack.

6. Creditor control and structure cannot be tested. The filings say a maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio exist and were met [S4 page:19], but give no levels; the credit agreement, its first amendment and the seller's exchange and registration agreements are not supplied. Management's own leverage measures use different definitions. The implication is that headroom, permitted distributions and the effect of a possible share overhang on equity market access (used four times since 2024 to fund acquisitions) are open.

runs.text: Earnings scale and margin (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the characterisations). VSE's Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 107.2 million in Q3 2026 at a margin of 19.8% against 16.7% a year earlier, and in Q3 2026 adjustments net to a small deduction (EBITDA of USD 107.6 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 107.2 million [S7 page:7]), so that margin is close to unadjusted; over nine months add-backs are about a tenth of adjusted EBITDA. Basis: CP-1 financials and credit metrics; CP-1A cost-of-sales margin rows. The mechanism is operating leverage from a repair-weighted mix, which supports debt service if sustained.

Equity-funded acquisition financing (Documentary Fact). About USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the PAG purchase, and unit holders' prepaid stock purchase contracts settle in shares in 2029, so the equity layer under the debt grew and the units add only USD 61.0 million of debt. Basis: CP-1A transaction summary; CP-1 debt table. This lowers debt-to-capitalisation (book debt about 24.7% of book debt plus equity, calculated below).

Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 545.0 million of liquidity, a revolver to 2030, and a term loan to 2033 with USD 9.0 million a year of amortization leave no large refinancing event until 2030, and then only the USD 20.0 million revolver draw. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts.

Diversified end markets with a repair moat (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is 98.9% commercial across airlines, cargo, MRO providers and owners, and FAA-certified repair capacity and OEM licenses are barriers to entry. Basis: CP-1A company and operating model rows. The mechanism is aftermarket demand tied to fleet usage rather than new deliveries.

Cash conversion (Documentary Fact). Nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million after a USD 148.4 million inventory build, with inventories at about 19.9% of total assets. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A working capital row. A stalled OEM program would raise net debt while earnings look stable.

Leverage and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA, with about USD 667.8 million of unhedged floating debt. Basis: CP-1 leverage and liquidity figures. Rising rates or an earnings miss would compress cover; covenant levels are unknown.
Customer and OEM concentration (Documentary Fact). A single customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and PAG's customer mix is not disclosed. Basis: CP-1A concentration row.

Acquired-asset and integration risk (Documentary Fact). Goodwill and intangibles are 62.6% of total assets, tangible equity is only USD 178.7 million, purchase accounting is preliminary for several deals, and internal controls are being integrated. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A integration row. This limits balance-sheet support in a stress and increases impairment risk if acquired earnings disappoint; it is a mechanic, not a recovery view.

Opaque creditor protections (Insufficient Information). Covenant levels, guarantor and security details, and seller-agreement terms are Not supplied, which matters for headroom, structural position and distributions.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transaction that defines the period is the acquisition of Precision Aviation Group (PAG), a portfolio company of GenNx360 Capital Partners, under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2026-01-29 and completed on 2026-05-05. Status: completed. The parties named in the executed agreement listing are VSE Corporation, two VSE acquisition vehicles, GenNx/PAG IntermediateCo Inc. and GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC (S1 page:79); a first amendment to the agreement dated 2026-05-04, an exchange and redemption agreement, a registration rights agreement and two lock-up agreements, all dated 2026-05-05 and all with GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC, are listed as exhibits (S3 page:33), but none of those documents is in the pack, so their terms are Insufficient Information. The second-quarter 10-Q summarises the deal as total consideration of "approximately $2.02 billion" (S3 page:9). The 10-K and the first-quarter 10-Q describe total upfront consideration of approximately USD 2.025 billion, in the Q1 10-Q "consisting of $1.750 billion in cash" plus an in-kind payment of 1,415,752 shares of newly issued equity of a VSE subsidiary, with up to USD 125.0 million of contingent earn-out on PAG's 2026 adjusted EBITDA (S1 page:73; S2 page:20). The later 10-Qs record total purchase consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand: cash paid 1,770,370, less cash acquired 22,215, equity at fair value 238,002 and an earn-out at acquisition-date fair value of 33,850 (S3 page:9; S4 page:9 and page:10). These are two bases for the same deal and are logged as a conflict below, not reconciled.

Use of proceeds and sources. The cash price was funded by a February 2026 common stock offering of 4,587,766 shares at USD 188.00 per share (net proceeds USD 829.0 million) and a tangible equity unit offering of 9,200,000 units at a stated USD 50.00 each (net proceeds USD 444.9 million), together about USD 1.3 billion net, plus borrowings of USD 900.0 million under a new term loan B (S4 page:26 and page:29; S2 page:20). Each unit combines a prepaid stock purchase contract, settled in shares on 2029-02-01 within a range of 0.2171 to 0.2660 shares per contract, and a senior unsecured amortizing note paying 5.93% per annum with final installment on 2029-02-01 (S4 page:19, page:26 and page:27). The new debt issues are therefore the term loan B (USD 900.0 million, due 2033-05-05, status: funded 2026-05-05, USD 897.75 million outstanding at 2026-09-30), the revolver upsize from USD 400.0 million to USD 500.0 million (due 2030-05-02, USD 20.0 million drawn at 2026-09-30) and the amortizing notes (USD 61.043 million outstanding at 2026-09-30); the prior term loan was repaid in full, and a debt commitment letter whose bridge and backstop commitments "were reduced to $0" had been signed with the purchase agreement (S4 page:18; S1 page:29). Debt issuance costs of USD 20.8 million were incurred on the amendment (S4 page:18). Liquidity effect and leverage after the deal are in the prior handoff (CP-1): principal debt of USD 978.8 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 296.3 million at 2025-12-31.

Other transactions. Atech Turbine Components, acquired on 2026-08-31 for USD 64.1 million net of cash acquired and funded with cash and revolver borrowings; NorthStar Technologies, acquired on 2026-04-01 for USD 10.1 million; Aero 3, acquired on 2025-12-23 for USD 346.1 million as revised (S2 stated 346.4); each is described as not material or preliminary (S4 page:9, page:12 and page:13). Subsequent event: Test Logic, Inc. was acquired on 2026-10-05, funded with cash on hand, price not disclosed (S4 page:27). Transaction-related status risks: the PAG, Atech, NorthStar and Aero 3 purchase price allocations are preliminary (S4 page:9 to page:15).

Ownership and control. VSE is a public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder named in the filings or the context; beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information. After closing, the PAG seller holds 1,415,752 shares of a VSE subsidiary, exchangeable at any time and automatically exchanged into Company common stock on a one-for-one basis if not exchanged by 2029-05-05, "subject to a lock-up period" whose length is not stated (S4 page:10). That makes the seller a potential holder of a significant block once exchanged; its percentage of common stock is not stated and is not inferred here.

fields.value: The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested work. Every period the run needs is covered by a filed statement: FY2025 audited (S1) and Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 unaudited (S2, S3, S4), each with balance sheet, operations, cash flow and notes, plus three earnings releases (S5, S6, S7) that supply discrete quarters, non-GAAP reconciliations, net debt and leverage tables, and guidance. The strongest contrary evidence is that the legal documents behind the debt are absent: the registrant states a maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio but never prints a level, and the May 2026 amendment that created the USD 900.0 million term loan B is described only in the notes. That does not stop the financial, business or credit work, but it blocks covenant headroom, guarantor and security analysis and any claim about definitions in the credit agreement. The second limitation is perimeter: the Precision Aviation Group acquisition on 2026-05-05 contributed USD 173.7 million of Q3 2026 revenue of USD 541.0 million (S4 page:29 and page:30), so FY2025 and the first four months of 2026 describe a different business from Q3 2026, and the acquisition accounting is preliminary. The next evidence action is to obtain the credit agreement dated 2025-05-02, the first amendment dated 2026-05-05, and the amortizing-note terms, and to have each consumer use filed statements ahead of release figures wherever the two differ.

fields.value: Entity and perimeter. All seven sources report VSE Corporation consolidated (single reportable segment, Aviation: S4 page:21 "manages its business as a single reportable and operating segment"). No parent, sponsor or stand-alone borrower statements exist; the context names no borrower, parent or guarantors. The borrower under the credit agreement is the Company, with subsidiary guarantors, per the exhibit list (S1 page:81 "10.8 Credit Agreement, dated as of May 2, 2025"), but no source names the guarantors, so the restricted or guaranteeing group is an unresolved distinction. The seller of the acquired target was paid partly in newly issued equity of an unnamed VSE subsidiary (S4 page:10, 1,415,752 shares, exchangeable one-for-one into Company common stock by 2029-05-05); that subsidiary is not identified.

fields.value: The three 10-Qs and the 10-K are successive periods, not versions of one another; each stays an active source. The three releases are management documents and each stays active. Where a release and a filing differ, the filing controls and the release is an attributed claim. The differences found are listed here with locators and their effect.

fields.value: Net debt as the releases define it deducts debt issuance costs as well as cash (S7 page:5 "Net debt is defined as principal amount of debt less debt issuance costs and less cash and cash equivalents"). That is a management definition and differs from principal less cash; consumers must state which they use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the debt: S4 page:19 gives the maturity table by facility, "Total $ 897,750 $ 20,000 $ 61,043 $ 978,793", which is a filed statement and fully supports the facility-level debt and maturity-wall work; the risk is only that the instrument terms behind it (guarantees, security, covenant levels) are not in the pack, so CP-2 must describe those as stated by the registrant and not test them. Second, liquidity: S4 page:32 states "$479.2 million of unused commitments under the Credit Agreement" and S4 page:17 gives letters of credit and interest rates, so liquidity can be built from filed inputs; the amount of any facility expiring within twelve months is answerable from the maturity dates in S4 page:18 (revolver 2030-05-02, term loan 2033-05-05). Third, earnings quality: the Q3 results are the first full quarter with the acquired business, so Q3 2026 is not a run-rate-comparable quarter to any 2025 quarter; the only acquisition-adjusted earnings measure is a management figure with no schedule (S7 page:5 "does not reflect all adjustments that would otherwise be required in connection with the preparation of pro forma financial statements"), so CP-1 and CP-2 must label it as management-attributed and not use it as audited or pro forma. Fourth, contingent items: the earn-out to the seller carries a maximum of USD 125.0 million payable in cash or equity at the Company's option (S4 page:10), and the Fleet sale earn-out receivable of up to USD 65.0 million was carried at nil after a USD 29.2 million fair value write-down in 2025, and its preliminary results show the threshold was not achieved (S4 page:25 "the earn-out performance threshold was not achieved"); both are note disclosures consumers must carry.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot, and it describes a business that changed shape during 2026. Revenue and earnings are strong and the filed statements are complete for every period needed, but the perimeter now includes the Precision Aviation Group business acquired on 2026-05-05, which contributed USD 173.7 million of the USD 541.0 million of Q3 2026 revenue, so FY2025 and Q3 2026 are not like-for-like. The acquisition took debt from USD 296.3 million to USD 978.8 million of principal while about USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the cash price (S4 page:29); net debt over management's trailing adjusted EBITDA is 3.04x, or 2.35x if management's pre-acquisition earnings are accepted, against 1.24x at the end of 2025. Liquidity is adequate, and the debt is mostly secured floating-rate bank debt maturing in 2030 and 2033. The weak points are cash conversion (nine-month free cash flow negative after a large inventory build), a quarter with a non-cash earn-out gain inside operating income, add-backs of about a tenth of nine-month adjusted EBITDA, and the absence of covenant levels. Those points limit confidence in leverage trajectory and headroom, not in the reported balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reporting entity is VSE Corporation consolidated (S4 page:21, single reportable segment, Aviation); there is no stand-alone borrower, parent or sponsor statement, and the context names none. The borrower under the credit agreement is the Company, with subsidiary guarantors named only generically in the exhibit list (S1 page:81 "each subsidiary of the Company from time to time party thereto as guarantors"). Amounts are continuing operations unless marked. The cash flow statement still combines continuing and discontinued operations for 2025 comparatives (S7 page:12 "The cash flows related to discontinued operations and held-for-sale assets and liabilities have not been segregated"), so 2025 operating cash flow and free cash flow include the Fleet business until its April 2025 sale. Periods used: FY2025, Q1 to Q3 2026 and Q3 2025, nine months (9M) 2025 and 2026, and trailing twelve months (TTM) as management prints them.

Interest rate swaps designated as cash flow hedges hedge USD 250.0 million of notional: USD 150.0 million at 2.8% through 2027-10-31 and USD 100.0 million at 4.0% through 2029-07-31 (S4 page:19), against USD 917.75 million of floating-rate secured debt. The prepaid stock purchase contracts in the units are equity, settled in shares on 2029-02-01 (S4 page:26 and page:27), and carry no cash claim.

The sum is 978.793, equal to total principal. Almost 87% of principal falls in 2032 or later (850.5 of 978.8, calculated below). fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure. For 9M 2026 it adds 27,084 to EBITDA of 221,535 to reach 248,619 (S7 page:7): acquisition, integration and restructuring costs 18,431, stock-based compensation 12,992, a loss on debt extinguishment 4,473 and divestiture-related costs 68, less an earn-out fair value gain of 8,880. The add-backs are about 10.9% of Adjusted EBITDA. In Q3 2026 the earn-out gain of 8,880 is deducted in the bridge from EBITDA of 107,581 to Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165, together with 4,059 of acquisition costs and 4,405 of stock compensation (S7 page:7), but it remains inside reported operating income of 77,451 and net income of 47,264. Q3 2025 shows the opposite: a 23,300 earn-out charge depressed reported operating income of 10,087 (S4 page:4). Comparing Q3 2026 with Q3 2025 reported earnings therefore overstates the underlying change; Adjusted EBITDA of 107,165 against 47,351 is the cleaner comparison but is still a management figure and still mixes perimeters (PAG contributed 173,666 of Q3 2026 revenue, S4 page:30). The retained quarters tie: Q1 55,430 plus Q2 86,024 equals H1 2026 of 141,454 (S6 page:7), and H1 plus Q3 107,165 equals the 9M 2026 figure of 248,619.

Free cash flow was negative 3,415 for 9M 2026 and positive 46,619 in Q3 2026 (S7 page:7); the Q3 figure alone cannot be annualised. Management expects "strong fourth quarter free cash flow" (S7 page:2), a forward statement the filings do not evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE is a single-segment aviation aftermarket business that sells parts (distribution) and repairs components and engines (repair), and in 2026 it bought its way into a larger engine-repair and distribution platform. The strongest support for a creditor is that the largest deal, Precision Aviation Group (PAG), was funded with a large equity raise and tangible equity units alongside a USD 900.0 million term loan B, that PAG already contributes about a third of quarterly revenue, and that the group has raised equity repeatedly since 2024 to fund acquisitions. The weakest points are concentration (one affiliated customer group at about 20% of FY2025 revenue), dependence on OEM licenses and approvals for the highest-value repairs, and an acquisition pace that leaves purchase accounting preliminary for several deals at once. What decides the outcome is integration of PAG and the Q4 2026 cash flow, because debt now rests mostly on floating-rate bank facilities, and because the documents that govern control rights (credit agreement, purchase agreement amendment, exchange and registration agreements) are not in the pack. Management's characterisations (record results, leading position, sole-source repairs) are quoted as Management Language below and are not adopted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction that defines the period is the acquisition of Precision Aviation Group (PAG), a portfolio company of GenNx360 Capital Partners, under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2026-01-29 and completed on 2026-05-05. Status: completed. The parties named in the executed agreement listing are VSE Corporation, two VSE acquisition vehicles, GenNx/PAG IntermediateCo Inc. and GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC (S1 page:79); a first amendment to the agreement dated 2026-05-04, an exchange and redemption agreement, a registration rights agreement and two lock-up agreements, all dated 2026-05-05 and all with GenNx360 PAG Buyer, LLC, are listed as exhibits (S3 page:33), but none of those documents is in the pack, so their terms are Insufficient Information. The second-quarter 10-Q summarises the deal as total consideration of "approximately $2.02 billion" (S3 page:9). The 10-K and the first-quarter 10-Q describe total upfront consideration of approximately USD 2.025 billion, in the Q1 10-Q "consisting of $1.750 billion in cash" plus an in-kind payment of 1,415,752 shares of newly issued equity of a VSE subsidiary, with up to USD 125.0 million of contingent earn-out on PAG's 2026 adjusted EBITDA (S1 page:73; S2 page:20). The later 10-Qs record total purchase consideration of USD 2,020,007 thousand: cash paid 1,770,370, less cash acquired 22,215, equity at fair value 238,002 and an earn-out at acquisition-date fair value of 33,850 (S3 page:9; S4 page:9 and page:10). These are two bases for the same deal and are logged as a conflict below, not reconciled.

fields.value: Use of proceeds and sources. The cash price was funded by a February 2026 common stock offering of 4,587,766 shares at USD 188.00 per share (net proceeds USD 829.0 million) and a tangible equity unit offering of 9,200,000 units at a stated USD 50.00 each (net proceeds USD 444.9 million), together about USD 1.3 billion net, plus borrowings of USD 900.0 million under a new term loan B (S4 page:26 and page:29; S2 page:20). Each unit combines a prepaid stock purchase contract, settled in shares on 2029-02-01 within a range of 0.2171 to 0.2660 shares per contract, and a senior unsecured amortizing note paying 5.93% per annum with final installment on 2029-02-01 (S4 page:19, page:26 and page:27). The new debt issues are therefore the term loan B (USD 900.0 million, due 2033-05-05, status: funded 2026-05-05, USD 897.75 million outstanding at 2026-09-30), the revolver upsize from USD 400.0 million to USD 500.0 million (due 2030-05-02, USD 20.0 million drawn at 2026-09-30) and the amortizing notes (USD 61.043 million outstanding at 2026-09-30); the prior term loan was repaid in full, and a debt commitment letter whose bridge and backstop commitments "were reduced to $0" had been signed with the purchase agreement (S4 page:18; S1 page:29). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: VSE Corporation is a profitable aviation aftermarket credit that has become much larger and materially more leveraged, and its credit quality now depends on integrating the Precision Aviation Group business and turning earnings into cash. The strongest support is earnings growth, with a record Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.8% in Q3 2026, liquidity of USD 545.0 million and annual scheduled principal of no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031. The weakest point is cash conversion: free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million for the nine months to September 2026 while net debt stands at 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA and the covenant levels are unknown. Delivery of the fourth-quarter cash flow management expects, with margins holding, decides the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. VSE has levered up through an equity-heavy acquisition, and its leverage path is mostly a matter of earnings timing. Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA against 1.24x at December 2025 [CP-1 leverage chart; S7 page:7], because the trailing earnings include only five months of the acquired business while all of its debt is on the balance sheet. Management's full-year 2026 guidance of revenue growth of 65% to 66.5% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.9% to 19.1% [S7 page:3] implies full-year Adjusted EBITDA of about USD 347 million to USD 354 million (calculated below), which would put net debt at about 2.6x on a flat net debt. This is a mechanical, not a proven, deleveraging, and it relies on guidance that the filings do not yet evidence (Analyst Interpretation on a Management Language basis). The credit implication is that leverage tolerance is acceptable if the guided run-rate is delivered and thin if the acquired earnings disappoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. VSE's liquidity and maturity profile make near-term default or refinancing risk low. Cash of USD 65.8 million and unused revolver commitments of USD 479.2 million total USD 545.0 million against USD 32.3 million of principal due within twelve months, and annual scheduled principal is no more than USD 34.1 million through 2031, with the balance of the term loan due from 2032, mostly at its 2033 maturity [CP-1 maturity wall; S4 page:19]. The risk mechanic that remains is acquisition spending: the revolver helps fund bolt-on deals (Atech, acquired on 2026-08-31, was funded with cash and revolver borrowings, and USD 20.0 million was drawn at 2026-09-30 [S4 page:9 and page:17]) so liquidity can fall if acquisitions continue before free cash flow turns up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Cash conversion is the weak spot. Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months and free cash flow negative USD 3.4 million, after a USD 148.4 million inventory build [CP-1; S4 page:6], while Q3 2026 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million. Growth programs, including the new OEM auxiliary power unit program the Company names [S4 page:33], absorb inventory ahead of revenue. The credit implication is that debt reduction comes from year-end working capital release and earnings, not from structural cash generation shown so far; the write-down of slow-moving inventories was a critical audit matter in FY2025 [S1 page:40].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. VSE's cost of debt is floating and only partly hedged. Secured floating debt is USD 917.75 million with USD 250.0 million of swaps, leaving about USD 667.8 million exposed; each 100 bp rise adds roughly USD 6.7 million of annual interest, about 2.2% of trailing adjusted EBITDA (calculated below). Trailing adjusted EBITDA covers contractual annual interest of USD 57.7 million 5.20x. Cash interest cover cannot be shown for 2026 because cash interest is not reported (FY2025 was 6.81x) [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. The business risks are concentration and dependence on OEMs. One affiliated customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and its post-acquisition share is not disclosed [CP-1A; S1 page:11]; repair, now 58.8% of Q3 2026 revenue, depends on OEM approvals and licenses such as the Pratt & Whitney PT6 fuel pump license [CP-1A; S4 page:14]. The mechanism is that the loss of the group or an approval removes high-margin work while inventory and capacity remain. The implication is that earnings quality is exposed to two single points of failure whose terms are not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Creditor control and structure cannot be tested. The filings say a maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and a minimum Interest Coverage Ratio exist and were met [S4 page:19], but give no levels; the credit agreement, its first amendment and the seller's exchange and registration agreements are not supplied. Management's own leverage measures use different definitions. The implication is that headroom, permitted distributions and the effect of a possible share overhang on equity market access (used four times since 2024 to fund acquisitions) are open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings scale and margin (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the characterisations). VSE's Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 107.2 million in Q3 2026 at a margin of 19.8% against 16.7% a year earlier, and in Q3 2026 adjustments net to a small deduction (EBITDA of USD 107.6 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 107.2 million [S7 page:7]), so that margin is close to unadjusted; over nine months add-backs are about a tenth of adjusted EBITDA. Basis: CP-1 financials and credit metrics; CP-1A cost-of-sales margin rows. The mechanism is operating leverage from a repair-weighted mix, which supports debt service if sustained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity-funded acquisition financing (Documentary Fact). About USD 1.3 billion of net equity and tangible equity unit proceeds funded a portion of the PAG purchase, and unit holders' prepaid stock purchase contracts settle in shares in 2029, so the equity layer under the debt grew and the units add only USD 61.0 million of debt. Basis: CP-1A transaction summary; CP-1 debt table. This lowers debt-to-capitalisation (book debt about 24.7% of book debt plus equity, calculated below).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 545.0 million of liquidity, a revolver to 2030, and a term loan to 2033 with USD 9.0 million a year of amortization leave no large refinancing event until 2030, and then only the USD 20.0 million revolver draw. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversified end markets with a repair moat (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is 98.9% commercial across airlines, cargo, MRO providers and owners, and FAA-certified repair capacity and OEM licenses are barriers to entry. Basis: CP-1A company and operating model rows. The mechanism is aftermarket demand tied to fleet usage rather than new deliveries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion (Documentary Fact). Nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 3.4 million after a USD 148.4 million inventory build, with inventories at about 19.9% of total assets. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A working capital row. A stalled OEM program would raise net debt while earnings look stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Net debt is 3.04x trailing adjusted EBITDA, with about USD 667.8 million of unhedged floating debt. Basis: CP-1 leverage and liquidity figures. Rising rates or an earnings miss would compress cover; covenant levels are unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and OEM concentration (Documentary Fact). A single customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue and PAG's customer mix is not disclosed. Basis: CP-1A concentration row.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquired-asset and integration risk (Documentary Fact). Goodwill and intangibles are 62.6% of total assets, tangible equity is only USD 178.7 million, purchase accounting is preliminary for several deals, and internal controls are being integrated. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A integration row. This limits balance-sheet support in a stress and increases impairment risk if acquired earnings disappoint; it is a mechanic, not a recovery view.
